recommendation_summary: The reply recommends acting now: keep the current shared folder for drafts only and add a separate Approved folder. Authors get read-only access there and only reviewers can write. At approval, a reviewer saves a locked copy and logs the document, version, author, approver and date-time, and the copy is kept for 7 years. It adds no optional extras. It leaves some gaps: the log and locked copy rest on reviewer write access, there is no trusted timestamp, and reviewers could still overwrite copies.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Customer contract requires 7 year retention of exact approved version with approver identity and time, no self approval, and immutable approved copy; you asked to ship this week with folder plus initials.
labels.Deleted: Folder APPROVED column with typed initials and naming convention alone, because it gives no immutability, verifiable identity, trusted time, or segregation.
labels.Bottleneck: 12 authors can edit the shared folder and anyone can type initials, so an approval can be faked, overwritten, or lost.
labels.Checked myself: You stated 12 authors and 3 remote reviewers, authors can edit the current folder, and your preferred plan is keep folder plus initials.

note: Access controls on the separate Approved folder keep authors from approving or changing copies, and the logged identity, time and version plus 7-year retention meet LARGER, though leniently.
